collection.credit: NEW EVENTS — LUCK, OMENS AND LAVASTONES (LO-01 to LO-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)

ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)

collection.description: A teenager whistles after dark on purpose, and a gust of wind rattles every roof in the village.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The elders say you should never whistle after dark, because it calls the wind. (subject), a teenager, thinks that's silly. Tonight, sitting by the fire, (subject.he/she) whistles a tune, loudly, on purpose, looking straight at (friend), an elder. A moment later, a gust of wind rattles every roof in the village and blows sparks out of the fire.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: "Coincidence," says (subject), a bit too quickly. (friend) raises an eyebrow and says nothing. The wind dies down. (subject) doesn't whistle again that night. Or, (subject.he/she) notices, the next night. Not because (subject.he/she) believes it. (subject.He/She) just doesn't feel like whistling, that's all.

text_only.reason: death talked about or remembered in the story; nobody dies

b__fx.name: Answer B
b__fx.text: "Does it really call the wind?" asks (subject). (friend) thinks. "I don't know," (friend.he/she) says honestly. "My grandmother believed it. I've seen the wind come after whistling. I've seen it not come, too." (subject) thinks about this. "So you don't know either." "No. But I don't whistle after dark. It's polite, just in case." (subject) finds that oddly reassuring.
